docs.text: Other modules, such as taikai-kotlin, add rules to the group through configure(customizer, supplier). disable() removes them with the rest of the group.

docs.title: 14. Predefined Checks
docs.text:
Taikai ships custom checks for common project conventions in the package com.enofex.taikai.checks. Taikai does not register them itself, so that a new Taikai version never adds checks on its own. To run them, list the checks you want in the file src/test/resources/META-INF/services/com.enofex.taikai.checks.spi.TaikaiCheck of the project, next to any other checks:

com.enofex.taikai.checks.ClassFileVersionCheck
com.enofex.taikai.checks.FileContentCheck
com.enofex.taikai.checks.ForbiddenFilesCheck
com.enofex.taikai.checks.GradleWrapperCheck
com.enofex.taikai.checks.MavenWrapperCheck
com.enofex.taikai.checks.RequiredFilesCheck
com.enofex.taikai.checks.ServiceRegistrationsCheck

Then discover them with discoverChecks(). Checks with settings are configured by their class:

Taikai.builder()
    .namespace("com.company.project")
    .discoverChecks(checks -> checks
        .configure(RequiredFilesCheck.class, RequiredFilesCheck.files("README.md", "LICENSE"))
        .configure(ForbiddenFilesCheck.class,
            ForbiddenFilesCheck.files("src/main/**/*.key", "src/main/**/.env"))
        .configure(ClassFileVersionCheck.class, ClassFileVersionCheck.javaVersion(17)))
    .build()
    .checkAll();
Check Checks that Configuration ClassFileVersionCheck classes are not compiled for a newer Java version than allowed required FileContentCheck the content of the project files follows the configured rules required ForbiddenFilesCheck the project contains no forbidden files, such as private keys required GradleWrapperCheck the project has the Gradle Wrapper optional MavenWrapperCheck the project has the Maven Wrapper optional RequiredFilesCheck the project has the required files, none of them empty required ServiceRegistrationsCheck the META-INF/services registrations refer to valid providers optional

The checks that look at files resolve them against the project directory, which is the directory of the module under test. Every path in the settings of a check is relative to it. In a multi-module build, files such as the README or the Maven or Gradle Wrapper usually lie in the root directory instead, so point the settings of these checks there with .., while the other checks keep looking at the module:

.discoverChecks(checks -> checks
    .configure(RequiredFilesCheck.class, RequiredFilesCheck.files("../README.md", "../LICENSE"))
    .configure(MavenWrapperCheck.class, MavenWrapperCheck.directories(".."))
    .configure(ForbiddenFilesCheck.class, ForbiddenFilesCheck.files("src/main/**/*.key")))

docs.title: ClassFileVersionCheck
docs.text:
Classes should not be compiled for a newer Java version than configured

Reads the Java version from the header of every class file of the configuration and reports the classes compiled for a newer Java version than allowed. Classes imported from the namespace exclude test classes and the globally excluded classes; classes set with classes(...) are checked as given. Use it to keep a library usable on older Java versions, even when the build runs on a newer JDK. The check needs the newest allowed Java version:

.discoverChecks(checks -> checks
    .configure(ClassFileVersionCheck.class, ClassFileVersionCheck.javaVersion(17)))

Check: Classes should not be compiled for a newer Java version than configured
    Class com.company.project.OrderService is compiled for Java 21, but at most Java 17 is allowed

docs.title: FileContentCheck
docs.text:
Project files should follow the content rules

Checks the content of project files, for what the compiled classes do not show, such as imports, comments or source-only annotations. A rule applies to the files matching a glob pattern, as in the ForbiddenFilesCheck. The check needs its rules:

.discoverChecks(checks -> checks
    .configure(FileContentCheck.class, FileContentCheck.rules(
        FileContentCheck.forbid("src/main/**/*.java", "^import .*\\*;"),
        FileContentCheck.require("src/main/**/package-info.java", "@NullMarked"),
        FileContentCheck.rule("src/main/**/*.java", (file, content) -> content.lines().count() > 500
            ? List.of(file + " has more than 500 lines") : List.of()))))

forbid reports every line that matches, require every file that does not, and rule the violations of a custom Condition. In regular expressions, ^ and $ match at every line. Files are read as UTF-8; binary files are skipped.

Check: Project files should follow the content rules
    src/main/java/com/company/project/OrderService.java:3 contains forbidden content (matches ^import .*\*;)
    src/main/java/com/company/project/order/package-info.java does not contain required content (should match @NullMarked)

docs.title: ForbiddenFilesCheck
docs.text:
Project should not contain forbidden files

Reports files that must not be in the project, for example private keys or .env files. The files are glob patterns relative to the project directory, as in FileSystem.getPathMatcher(String). As in .gitignore, **/ also matches no directory, so **/.env also finds the .env in the project directory itself.

The check needs the patterns of the forbidden files. Patterns in src/main are a good start, because everything in there ends up in the artifact, whether it is committed or not: a key that .gitignore keeps out of the repository would still be packaged from there. src/test, on the other hand, often contains test keystores on purpose. A configuration for private keys and certificates, .env files, and compiled or packaged files could look like this:

.discoverChecks(checks -> checks
    .configure(ForbiddenFilesCheck.class, ForbiddenFilesCheck.files(
        "src/main/**/*.pem", "src/main/**/*.key", "src/main/**/*.p12", "src/main/**/*.jks",
        "src/main/**/.env", "src/main/**/*.class", "src/main/**/*.jar")))

Only the directory before the first wildcard of a pattern is searched, and only as deep as the pattern reaches, so src/main/**/*.key does not look into target or .git. A pattern such as **/.env searches the whole project directory, including files that .gitignore keeps out of the repository, such as a local .env. A pattern outside of the project directory starts with .., for example ../.env in the root of a multi-module build.

Check: Project should not contain forbidden files
    src/main/resources/server.key is forbidden (matches src/main/**/*.key)

docs.title: GradleWrapperCheck
docs.text:
Project should have the Gradle Wrapper

Checks that the project can be built without a local Gradle installation: the scripts gradlew and gradlew.bat and the files gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.jar and gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.properties must exist in the project directory and must not be empty.

The check needs no configuration. When the wrapper lies elsewhere, for example in the root of a multi-project build while the project directory is the subproject under test, configure its directories instead, relative to the project directory. Every configured directory must have the wrapper, so a repository with several builds can check all of them:

.discoverChecks(checks -> checks
    .configure(GradleWrapperCheck.class, GradleWrapperCheck.directories("..")))

Check: Project should have the Gradle Wrapper
    gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.jar is missing in /home/dev/project

docs.title: MavenWrapperCheck
docs.text:
Project should have the Maven Wrapper

Checks that the project can be built without a local Maven installation: the scripts mvnw and mvnw.cmd and the file .mvn/wrapper/maven-wrapper.properties must exist in the project directory and must not be empty.

The check needs no configuration. When the wrapper lies elsewhere, for example in the root of a multi-module build while the project directory is the module under test, configure its directories instead, relative to the project directory. Every configured directory must have the wrapper, so a repository with several builds can check all of them:

.discoverChecks(checks -> checks
    .configure(MavenWrapperCheck.class, MavenWrapperCheck.directories("..")))

Check: Project should have the Maven Wrapper
    mvnw.cmd is missing in /home/dev/project

docs.title: RequiredFilesCheck
docs.text:
Project should have the required files

Reports required files that are missing in the project directory or empty; a directory with the name of a required file counts as missing. The check needs the required files; their paths are relative to the project directory and may point into subdirectories, or with .. outside of it, for example to ../README.md in the root of a multi-module build:

.discoverChecks(checks -> checks
    .configure(RequiredFilesCheck.class,
        RequiredFilesCheck.files("README.md", "LICENSE", "SECURITY.md", ".github/CODEOWNERS")))

Check: Project should have the required files
    /home/dev/project/LICENSE is empty
    SECURITY.md is missing in /home/dev/project

A missing file outside of the project directory is reported with its path, such as /home/dev/README.md is missing.

docs.title: ServiceRegistrationsCheck
docs.text:
Service registrations should refer to valid providers

Checks the ServiceLoader registrations of the project, the files in src/main/resources/META-INF/services and src/test/resources/META-INF/services of the project directory. Every registered service must exist, and every provider must exist, implement the service, and be a public class with a public constructor without parameters, as the ServiceLoader requires. Comments and blank lines are ignored, and the classes are loaded with the class loader of the context without being initialized. Taikai uses it to validate its own registration of the predefined checks.

The check needs no configuration. A project directory without these directories has nothing to check, so the check passes. When the registrations lie elsewhere, configure the directories instead, relative to the project directory. Unlike the default directories, a configured directory must exist, so a wrong path is reported rather than silently checking nothing:

.discoverChecks(checks -> checks
    .configure(ServiceRegistrationsCheck.class, ServiceRegistrationsCheck.directories(
        "src/integration-test/resources/META-INF/services")))

Check: Service registrations should refer to valid providers
    Provider com.company.checks.LicenceCheck registered in src/test/resources/META-INF/services/com.enofex.taikai.checks.spi.TaikaiCheck does not exist

docs.title: 15. Recommended Starter Configuration
docs.text:
A reasonable baseline for a new Spring Boot project. It is deliberately conservative: every rule here is one most teams already agree on. Add the stricter rules once this passes.

class ArchitectureTest {

  @Test
  void architecture() {
    Taikai.builder()
        .namespace("com.company.project")
        .failOnEmpty(true)
        .java(java -> java
            .noUsageOfDeprecatedAPIs()
            .noUsageOfSystemOutOrErr()
            .fieldsShouldNotBePublic()
            .finalClassesShouldNotHaveProtectedMembers()
            .methodsShouldNotDeclareGenericExceptions()
            .utilityClassesShouldBeFinalAndHavePrivateConstructor()
            .serialVersionUIDFieldsShouldBeStaticFinalLong()
            .classesShouldImplementHashCodeAndEquals()
            .imports(imports -> imports
                .shouldHaveNoCycles()
                .shouldNotImport(ImportPatterns.shaded()))
            .naming(naming -> naming
                .packagesShouldMatchDefault()
                .classesShouldNotMatch(".*Impl")
                .constantsShouldFollowConventions()
                .enumConstantsShouldFollowConventions()
                .interfacesShouldNotHavePrefixI()))
        .logging(logging -> logging
            .loggersShouldFollowConventions(Logger.class, "logger", List.of(PRIVATE, FINAL)))
        .test(test -> test
            .junit(junit -> junit
                .classesShouldEndWithTest()
                .classesShouldBePackagePrivate(ClassCriteria.nameMatching(".*Test"))
                .classesShouldNotBeAnnotatedWithDisabled()
                .methodsShouldBePackagePrivate()
                .methodsShouldNotBeAnnotatedWithDisabled()
                .methodsShouldNotDeclareExceptions()
                .methodsShouldContainAssertionsOrVerifications()
                .testsShouldBeExecutable()))
        .spring(spring -> spring
            .noAutowiredFields()
            .noInjectionIntoStaticFields()
            .noSelfInvocationOfProxiedMethods()
            .boot(boot -> boot
                .applicationClassShouldResideInPackage())
            .configurations(configurations -> configurations
                .namesShouldEndWithConfiguration())
            .controllers(controllers -> controllers
                .namesShouldEndWithController()
                .shouldBeAnnotatedWithRestController()
                .shouldBePackagePrivate()
                .shouldNotDependOnOtherControllers()
                .shouldNotDependOnRepositories())
            .services(services -> services
                .namesShouldEndWithService()
                .shouldBeAnnotatedWithService()
                .shouldNotDependOnControllers())
            .repositories(repositories -> repositories
                .namesShouldEndWithRepository()
                .shouldBeAnnotatedWithRepository()
                .shouldNotDependOnServices()
                .shouldNotDependOnControllers())
            .transactional(transactional -> transactional
                .methodsShouldBePublic()
                .shouldNotBeSelfInvoked()
                .shouldNotBeUsedInControllers()))
        .build()
        .checkAll();
  }
}

Adopting this on an existing codebase will usually produce violations. Two ways to stage the rollout:

  • Run checkAll() to get the full list, then add the offenders to excludeClasses or a per-rule Configuration and work the list down.
  • Enable the rule groups one at a time, committing each as it goes green.

docs.title: 16. Complete Example
docs.text:
The configuration Taikai applies to its own codebase, from ArchitectureTest.java. Every rule and check runs as a test of its own:

import static com.enofex.taikai.java.ImportPatterns.lombok;
import static com.enofex.taikai.java.ImportPatterns.shaded;
import static com.tngtech.archunit.core.domain.JavaModifier.FINAL;
import static com.tngtech.archunit.core.domain.JavaModifier.STATIC;

class ArchitectureTest {

  @DisplayName("Should fulfill architecture constraints")
  @TestFactory
  Stream<DynamicTest> architecture() {
    return Taikai.builder()
        .namespace("com.enofex.taikai")
        .java(java -> java
            .noUsageOfDeprecatedAPIs()
            .noUsageOfSystemOutOrErr()
            .noUsageOf(Date.class)
            .noUsageOf(Calendar.class)
            .noUsageOf(SimpleDateFormat.class)
            .fieldsShouldHaveModifiers(FieldCriteria.nameMatching("^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*$"),
                List.of(STATIC, FINAL))
            .classesShouldImplementHashCodeAndEquals()
            .finalClassesShouldNotHaveProtectedMembers()
            .utilityClassesShouldBeFinalAndHavePrivateConstructor()
            .methodsShouldNotDeclareGenericExceptions()
            .fieldsShouldNotBePublic()
            .serialVersionUIDFieldsShouldBeStaticFinalLong()
            .classesShouldResideInPackage("com.enofex.taikai..")
            .imports(imports -> imports
                .shouldHaveNoCycles()
                .shouldNotImport(ClassCriteria.inPackage("org.springframework.core.annotation.."))
                .shouldNotImport(ClassCriteria.inPackage("jakarta.annotation.."))
                .shouldNotImport(ClassCriteria.inPackage("javax.annotation.."))
                .shouldNotImport(ClassCriteria.inPackage("org.jetbrains.annotations.."))
                .shouldNotImport(shaded())
                .shouldNotImport(lombok()))
            .naming(naming -> naming
                .packagesShouldMatchDefault()
                .fieldsShouldNotMatch(".*(List|Set|Map)$")
                .classesShouldNotMatch(".*Impl")
                .classesShouldMatch(ClassCriteria.assignableTo(AbstractConfigurer.class),
                    ".*Configurer")
                .classesShouldMatch(ClassCriteria.implementing(Configurer.class), ".*Configurer")
                .classesShouldMatch(ClassCriteria.implementing(TaikaiCheck.class), ".*Check")
                .classesShouldMatch(ClassCriteria.implementing(TaikaiExport.class), ".*Export")
                .classesShouldMatch(ClassCriteria.implementing(CheckContext.class),
                    ".*CheckContext")
                .classesShouldMatch(ClassCriteria.implementing(ExportContext.class),
                    ".*ExportContext")
                .interfacesShouldNotHavePrefixI()
                .enumConstantsShouldFollowConventions()
                .constantsShouldFollowConventions()))
        .metrics(metrics -> metrics
            .classesShouldNotExceedMaxInheritanceDepth(2)
            .packagesShouldNotExceedMaxClasses(20)
            .classesShouldNotExceedMaxDependencies(25))
        .discoverChecks(checks -> checks
            .configure(RequiredFilesCheck.class, RequiredFilesCheck.files(
                "../README.md", "../LICENSE", "../CONTRIBUTING.md", "../CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md",
                "../SECURITY.md"))
            .configure(MavenWrapperCheck.class, MavenWrapperCheck.directories(".."))
            .configure(ForbiddenFilesCheck.class, ForbiddenFilesCheck.files(
                "src/main/**/*.pem", "src/main/**/*.key", "src/main/**/*.p12", "src/main/**/*.jks",
                "src/main/**/.env", "src/main/**/*.class", "src/main/**/*.jar"))
            .configure(FileContentCheck.class, FileContentCheck.rules(
                FileContentCheck.forbid("src/main/**/*.java", "^import .*\\*;"),
                FileContentCheck.require("src/main/**/package-info.java",
                    "^@org\\.jspecify\\.annotations\\.NullMarked$")))
            .configure(ClassFileVersionCheck.class, ClassFileVersionCheck.javaVersion(17)))
        .build()
        .dynamicTests();
  }
}

The predefined checks are registered in src/test/resources/META-INF/services/com.enofex.taikai.checks.spi.TaikaiCheck:

com.enofex.taikai.checks.ClassFileVersionCheck
com.enofex.taikai.checks.FileContentCheck
com.enofex.taikai.checks.ForbiddenFilesCheck
com.enofex.taikai.checks.MavenWrapperCheck
com.enofex.taikai.checks.RequiredFilesCheck
com.enofex.taikai.checks.ServiceRegistrationsCheck

See the Spring Java demo for an HTTP application with its architecture tests and project checks.

docs.title: 17. Kotlin/JVM
docs.text: Taikai supports Kotlin callers and compiled Kotlin/JVM applications. The optional taikai-kotlin artifact adds source-aware rules and a receiver DSL without adding Kotlin dependencies to core. See the Kotlin manual for installation, all rules, Java rule compatibility, and the Spring Kotlin demo.

docs.title: Kotlin/JVM support
docs.text: Taikai can be called from Kotlin tests and can analyze compiled Kotlin/JVM code. Add taikai-kotlin for source-aware Kotlin rules and a receiver DSL. The existing taikai artifact remains Java-only and keeps its existing rule semantics. Kotlin/JS and Kotlin/Native are not supported.

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text:
Use the same Taikai version for both artifacts. taikai-kotlin brings core in transitively, so a separate core dependency is unnecessary.

<dependency>
  <groupId>com.enofex</groupId>
  <artifactId>taikai-kotlin</artifactId>
  <version>${taikai.version}</version>
  <scope>test</scope>
</dependency>

// build.gradle.kts
testImplementation("com.enofex:taikai-kotlin:$taikaiVersion")

Compile production Kotlin before running architecture tests. The Kotlin library, compiler fixtures, and metadata reader use Kotlin 2.3.21 and target JVM 17. Metadata from unsupported compiler versions produces an explicit failure identifying the class; it is never silently treated as compliant. Keep your resolved Kotlin runtime and metadata reader versions compatible with your application's compiler.

docs.title: Existing API from Kotlin
docs.text:
You do not need a new DSL to call the existing Java API:

import com.enofex.taikai.Taikai
import com.enofex.taikai.kotlin.kotlin
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test

class ArchitectureTest {
    @Test
    fun architecture() {
        Taikai.builder()
            .namespace("com.company.project")
            .spring { spring ->
                spring.services { it.namesShouldEndWithService() }
            }
            .kotlin {
                classesShouldBeDataClasses(".*Response")
                dataClassesShouldBeImmutable()
            }
            .build()
            .checkAll()
    }
}

docs.title: Receiver DSL
docs.text:
The taikai function builds a Taikai instance. It does not execute rules. Use check() to stop at the first failed rule or checkAll() to aggregate failures.

import com.enofex.taikai.kotlin.functionsShouldNotExceedMaxParameters
import com.enofex.taikai.kotlin.taikai

val architecture = taikai {
    namespace("com.company.project")
    failOnEmpty()
    java {
        fieldsShouldNotBePublic()
        classesShouldResideInPackage("com.company.project..")
    }
    spring {
        services { it.namesShouldEndWithService().shouldNotDependOnControllers() }
    }
    kotlin {
        classesShouldBeDataClasses(".*(Request|Response)")
        dataClassesShouldBeImmutable()
        functionsShouldMatch("[a-z][a-zA-Z0-9]*")
        propertiesShouldMatch("[a-z][a-zA-Z0-9]*")
    }
    metrics {
        functionsShouldNotExceedMaxParameters(4)
    }
}
architecture.checkAll()

java, spring, logging, test, quarkus, jpa, metrics, and kotlin blocks have configuration receivers. Nested Java configurers retain their existing callback API, as the services example shows. The DSL marker prevents accidental unqualified access to the outer builder inside these receiver blocks.

discoverChecks runs the project checks, with ChecksConfigurer as the receiver:

discoverChecks {
    configure(RequiredFilesCheck::class.java, RequiredFilesCheck.files("README.md", "LICENSE"))
}

discoverExports discovers the exports, with ExportsConfigurer as the receiver; export() on the built instance runs them:

taikai {
    namespace("com.company.project")
    discoverExports {
        configure(AgentsMarkdownExport::class.java, AgentsMarkdownExport.file("ARCHITECTURE.md"))
    }
}.export()

Use classes(MyType::class) or classes(importedJavaClasses) instead of a namespace for explicit imports. excludeClasses takes patterns such as "com.company.project.generated..", class literals such as Generated::class, or criteria. addRule(...), addRules(...), and failOnEmpty(false) are also available. Namespace and explicit classes remain mutually exclusive. Kotlin blocks can be repeated, and disable() clears previously registered Kotlin rules on that builder. toBuilder() preserves existing rules and allows new Kotlin rules without mutating the original instance; disable() on such a builder only clears the Kotlin rules added after toBuilder(), not the preserved ones.

docs.title: Kotlin-specific rules
docs.text:
All rules operate on Kotlin declarations only. Regexes match the entire simple source name, including names before JVM mangling; they are not package patterns. The class regex on requirement rules selects which Kotlin declarations to check.

Method Behavior classesShouldNotMatch(regex) Forbid matching source class names, excluding file facades and synthetic helpers. classesShouldMatch(regex) All source class names, including objects and companions, match the pattern. File facades and synthetic helpers are excluded. objectsShouldMatch(regex) Object and companion-object names match the pattern; other class kinds are ignored. functionsShouldNotMatch(regex) Forbid matching source function names, including names before internal JVM mangling. functionsShouldMatch(regex) Declared source function names match; accessors and generated data-class methods are excluded. propertiesShouldNotMatch(regex) Forbid matching non-constant property names, including computed and delegated properties. propertiesShouldMatch(type, regex) Require matching names for non-constant properties of the selected type; accepts a fully qualified type name, Java Class, or Kotlin KClass. Includes properties without backing fields. propertiesShouldMatch(regex) Declared non-constant property names match. A Boolean active property is checked as active, not getActive. noUsageOfDeprecatedAPIs() Forbid bytecode dependencies on deprecated classes and accesses to deprecated Kotlin or Java members, including property-level and accessor-level deprecation. constantsShouldFollowConventions() Only const val names must use uppercase letters, digits, and underscores, starting with a letter. Ordinary val properties and generated fields are excluded. classesShouldBeDataClasses(regex) Selected source classes must be data classes. dataClassesShouldBeImmutable() Data classes must declare only val properties, including properties outside their primary constructors. This does not enforce deep immutability of referenced objects or collections. classesShouldBeObjects(regex) Selected source classes must be regular object declarations. Companion objects do not satisfy this requirement. classesShouldHaveVisibility(regex, visibility) Selected class declarations have the specified source visibility. functionsShouldHaveVisibility(regex, visibility) Selected declared functions have the specified source visibility. propertiesShouldHaveVisibility(regex, visibility) Selected declared properties have the specified source visibility. Accessor visibility is not checked separately.

metrics { functionsShouldNotExceedMaxParameters(max) } counts declared function value parameters, excluding receivers, suspend continuations, default-argument machinery, generated overloads, and constructors. Import it from com.enofex.taikai.kotlin.

Visibility uses KotlinVisibility.PUBLIC, INTERNAL, PROTECTED, or PRIVATE. For example, functionsShouldHaveVisibility("load.*", KotlinVisibility.INTERNAL) checks source internal functions despite their public, mangled JVM representation. Only directly declared properties and functions are checked; inherited and delegated members are excluded. Explicitly declared overrides are included.

Each rule accepts an optional final TaikaiRule.Configuration, following core's namespace, import-mode, explicit-class, and exclusion behavior:

import com.enofex.taikai.Namespace
import com.enofex.taikai.TaikaiRule.Configuration

// Include test classes in this individual rule.
functionsShouldMatch(
    "[a-z][a-zA-Z0-9]*",
    Configuration.of("com.company.project", Namespace.IMPORT.WITH_TESTS),
)

The default excludes test classes. Empty selections pass unless failOnEmpty(true) is enabled. For Kotlin rules this checks the enclosing imported Kotlin-class selection; it does not require that a member-name/type filter selects a declaration. An unreadable metadata annotation on an included Kotlin class is a rule violation. Application classes are analyzed through imported annotation data and are not initialized to inspect metadata.

docs.title: Applying a shared Java architecture profile to Kotlin
docs.text:
Keep bytecode-level rules in java {} and use Kotlin declaration rules for source names, properties, and Kotlin deprecation. This profile expresses the conventions without treating file facades as Java utility classes or every static final field as a Kotlin constant:

import com.enofex.taikai.java.ImportPatterns
import com.enofex.taikai.kotlin.taikai

taikai {
    namespace("com.company.project")
    java {
        methodsShouldNotDeclareGenericExceptions()
        imports {
            it.shouldHaveNoCycles().shouldNotImport(ImportPatterns.shaded())
        }
        naming {
            it.enumConstantsShouldFollowConventions().interfacesShouldNotHavePrefixI()
        }
    }
    kotlin {
        noUsageOfDeprecatedAPIs()
        classesShouldNotMatch(".*Impl")
        functionsShouldNotMatch("^(foo|bar)$")
        propertiesShouldNotMatch(".*(List|Set|Map)$")
        propertiesShouldMatch("com.company.project.Matcher", "matcher")
        constantsShouldFollowConventions()
        classesShouldBeObjects(".*(?:Utils|Utilities)")
    }
}.checkAll()

methodsShouldNotDeclareGenericExceptions() checks JVM declarations produced by @Throws; it does not inspect arbitrary exceptions thrown by function bodies. The classesShouldBeObjects policy applies only to selected named containers; ordinary top-level functions do not need a private constructor.

Type-selected property naming uses exact source classifiers or erased JVM types, not subtype assignability. Nullable reference properties and generic arguments do not prevent matching. Kotlin KClass arguments also recognize the corresponding JVM type, such as List::class selecting MutableList properties through java.util.List. Int::class selects nullable and non-nullable Kotlin Int properties; Java Class arguments use the exact JVM representation. String inputs can specify either a Kotlin classifier (kotlin.String) or JVM name (java.lang.String). Kotlin source aliases are matched by their expanded type. Inherited and generated forwarding properties are excluded, consistently with other Kotlin property rules. Each overload accepts the final per-rule Configuration argument.

The Kotlin deprecation rule examines both kotlin.Deprecated and java.lang.Deprecated, including annotations on property carriers and individual accessors. It checks calls, member references, field accesses, and dependencies on deprecated classes. It follows default-argument helpers and generated callable reference adapters, preserving overload signatures. Companion and interface-property annotation carriers and generated adapters are read from their exact class resources without initializing application classes. Normal backing-field initialization and generated forwarding to a deprecated declaration do not turn the declaration itself into an API usage. Deprecated API calls inside default-value expressions are still checked.

The rule examines compiled bytecode. Inlined function bodies, inlined constants, and erased type aliases cannot reliably reveal that a deprecated source API was referenced. Kotlin's own compiler deprecation checks remain useful for these cases. The existing Java deprecation rule retains its original semantics; use the Kotlin rule for Kotlin callers of both Java and Kotlin APIs.

docs.title: Existing rule compatibility
docs.text:
These categories describe intended semantics; they do not promise that every individual rule in a category has Kotlin-specific coverage.

Existing rule category Kotlin/JVM behavior Package placement and dependency boundaries Shared bytecode rules work across Java and Kotlin. The suite verifies package placement and cross-language dependencies. Spring class annotations and naming Shared rules work for Kotlin Spring classes. The demo verifies controller/service/repository names and layer dependencies. Class inheritance and JVM modifiers Operate on compiled JVM declarations. Kotlin source visibility and default finality can differ from Java conventions. Fields and properties Java field rules inspect backing fields, not source properties. Prefer Kotlin property rules for source intent. Boolean method naming Java rules can reject the generated getActive() accessor. Prefer Kotlin function/property naming rules. Deprecation The Java rule checks Java deprecation annotations. The Kotlin rule handles Kotlin and Java deprecation, including source-property carriers and default helpers. Method parameter counts The metrics rule methodsShouldNotExceedMaxParameters counts JVM parameters. Prefer the Kotlin counterpart for suspend, extension, and default-argument functions. Utility classes and constants Java static-member conventions do not map cleanly to file facades, companions, objects, and ordinary val properties. Use Kotlin object and constant rules. Logging, framework methods, test methods Retain JVM semantics; annotation use-site targets, accessors, generated methods, and suspend signatures may matter. No automatic source adaptation is applied. Dependency cycles and forbidden dependencies Include compiler-generated dependencies. Helpers are not globally removed from imported classes.

Kotlin rules read metadata with the official Kotlin Metadata JVM library. The Kotlin/JVM interoperability documentation explains how source properties, companions, and top-level functions map to JVM members.

docs.title: Java callers and extensions
docs.text:
Java users can configure the optional rules without Kotlin extension functions:

Taikai.builder()
    .namespace("com.company.project")
    .configure(kotlin -> kotlin
        .classesShouldBeDataClasses(".*Response")
        .dataClassesShouldBeImmutable(), KotlinConfigurer::new)
    .build()
    .checkAll();

Import com.enofex.taikai.kotlin.KotlinConfigurer. The public generic Builder.configure(customizer, factory) extension point uses the same per-configurer registration and accumulation behavior as the built-in configuration methods.
